Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexCart Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions apply.] I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexCart Holdings' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; and Riley Patel, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexCart Holdings.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust growth in gross merchandise value, enhanced operational efficiencies, and expanding high-margin services for our sellers. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV up 22% year-over-year to $28.5 billion and active sellers surpassing 2.8 million.

Our focus remains on scaling our multi-category platform across fashion, consumer electronics, home goods, and beyond, while powering over 50 million annual orders for more than 15,000 merchant partners. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-driven Revenue Optimization Platform and expanded Nexus Fulfillment Network, which we believe will significantly boost take rates and fulfillment efficiencies.

We are investing heavily in automation, regional network densification, and data-centric marketing to drive sustainable leverage.

Finally, we are committed to delivering long-term value through disciplined profitability, with seller services emerging as a key flywheel.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $6.5 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by fulfillment cost improvements, take rate expansion, and higher-margin seller services. Operating expenses were $4.2 billion, representing 65% of revenue. Our marketing spend remained efficient, with ROAS at 5.2x and CAC trends showing continued optimization.

Our net income for the quarter was $650 million, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $25-26 billion in revenue and 14-15% adjusted EBITDA margins.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call for NexCart Holdings, your leading mid-market e-commerce platform. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our core operational and financial metrics, starting with fulfillment cost per order, or FCPO. This metric captures the full spectrum of our end-to-end fulfillment expenses, including inbound logistics to our 28 North American and European fulfillment centers, warehouse labor for picking and packing, packaging materials, outbound carrier fees, and last-mile delivery—excluding returns, which we track separately under net fulfillment costs.

The headline numbers underscore our relentless focus on operational leverage in a maturing post-pandemic e-commerce landscape. In Q3 2024, our blended FCPO came in at $7.18, marking a 15.3% year-over-year decline from $8.48 in Q3 2023 and a sequential improvement of 4.3% from the prior quarter. As a percentage of GMV, FCPO improved to 8.2% from 9.7% YoY, even as our average order value held steady at $92 amid softer consumer spending on discretionary categories like apparel. This outperformance versus peers—think Shopify's Fulfillment Network reporting FCPO north of $9 or BigCommerce partners averaging $8.50—stems from our scale advantages and targeted investments, allowing us to capture margin expansion as GMV grew 22% YoY to $28.5 billion.

Our FCPO trajectory reflects three phases over the past 24 months: first, the inflationary spike in 2022-early 2023, where FCPO peaked at $9.12, driven by 25%+ surges in parcel rates from UPS and FedEx amid capacity constraints and fuel costs averaging $4.50/gallon; labor costs ballooned 18% YoY due to warehouse wage inflation in high-velocity hubs like our Dallas and Rotterdam FCs. We clawed back aggressively through carrier renegotiations—locking in 12-15% discounts on ground and smart post volumes—and headcount optimization via attrition, bringing FCPO down significantly by year-end.

Q3 acceleration to $7.18 was fueled by efficiency gains outpacing volume growth. On a unit basis, outbound shipping costs dropped 18% YoY to $4.25 per order (59% of FCPO), warehouse fulfillment fell 12% to $2.12 (29%), and packaging/other dipped 8% to $0.81 (12%). Sequential pressure from lighter prior volumes was offset by fixed-cost leverage: our network throughput hit 1.8 million units per FC on average, up 28% YoY, diluting overheads like facility leases and depreciation.

Key drivers include technical initiatives. We've accelerated our automation roadmap, deploying 450 autonomous mobile robots—similar to Boston Dynamics' Stretch but customized via our partnership with Locus Robotics—in 12 of our highest-velocity FCs handling 70% of US volume. This slashed pick-and-pack cycle times by 32%, from 45 to 30 minutes per order, directly cutting labor costs by $0.45 per unit. Complementing this, we've rolled out AI-powered sortation systems from Honeywell in five sites, boosting throughput by 25% during peak hours and reducing mispicks by 40%, which inflated rework costs previously.

Demand forecasting has been a game-changer: our proprietary ML models, integrated with Snowflake for real-time SKU velocity analytics, improved inbound accuracy to 96% from 88% YoY, minimizing excess inventory handling costs. For high-SKU categories like electronics (partnering merchants selling Anker chargers or Dyson appliances), zone picking with AR glasses from Upskill reduced errors by 22%. On the last-mile front, dynamic routing via Bringg's platform optimized 85% of deliveries, yielding 11% savings on carrier fees by consolidating routes and shifting 15% of volume to economical USPS Ground Advantage amid softening diesel prices now at $3.80/gallon.

Regionally, North America, driving 68% of Q3 orders, hit FCPO at an industry-best $6.42—down 17% YoY—thanks to eight regional FCs and micro-fulfillment centers in Chicago, LA, and Atlanta. These MFCs, averaging 50,000 sq ft, enable 65% same-day/next-day fulfillment for Prime-like merchants, compressing last-mile costs to $2.10 vs. $3.20 for national hubs. Fuel normalization and our UPS Volume Service Incentive Program contract, securing 20% off-list rates, were tailwinds.

Europe, at 25% of volume, saw FCPO at $8.76—improved 11% YoY but lagging NA due to fragmentation; VAT complexities and stricter ESG regs on packaging added $0.30/unit, yet our new Warsaw FC and DHL eCommerce partnership cut cross-border times by 18 hours, saving 9% on express fees. Internationally (7% of volume, APAC-heavy), FCPO at $10.45 declined 14% YoY through Lazada and Shopee integrations, routing 60% via their networks at blended $4.50 last-mile rates.

Strategically, these gains position us for 12-15% annual improvements through 2026, even as same-day delivery penetration ramps from 22% to 35%. We're prioritizing sustainability: reusable totes now cover 45% of apparel orders, trimming packaging by 22% or $0.18/unit. Capex for automation remains at 4% of revenue, with ROI averaging 18 months. Q4 FCPO guidance is $7.05-$7.15, assuming stable carrier rates; risks include UFLPA enforcement or labor tightness, but $450 million in expansions prime us for 200-300bps gross margin expansion.

Next, let's unpack our take rate dynamics, which came in at 21.2% for the quarter—up 150 basis points year-over-year from 19.7% and 40 basis points sequentially. This marks our strongest quarterly expansion in three years, driving 28% of total revenue growth on a 15% GMV increase. This outperforms Shopify's 2.8% on GPV and positions us closer to MercadoLibre's 22-24% blended rate.

Pricing discipline contributed 90 basis points: we selectively repriced commissions in electronics (32% of GMV), increasing seller fees to 18% from 17.5%, justified by NFN adoption at 65%. Our AI-driven ROP analyzes elasticity from 1.2 million sellers, dynamically adjusting fees.

Promotions added 40 basis points as intensity fell to 14.2% of GMV from 18.5%, with PromoGuard AI throttling flash sales; effective promo take rate at 16.8%. Mix shifts drove 20 basis points: high-take verticals like home & garden (24.5%) grew faster. Regionally, NA expanded 120bps to 20.9%, APAC 220bps to 23.4%, EMEA flat at 21.0%, LatAm 180bps to 22.7%.

Advertising lifted blended take by 50bps, RPMs up 15% to $4.20; ROP recommends budgets at 2.5x ROAS. Q4 take rate guidance: 21.5-21.8%.

Turning to advertising and marketing spend efficiency, our ROAS was 5.2x, up 12% YoY from 4.65x and 8% sequentially from 4.8x. This drove $1.2 billion revenue from $150 million spend (12% of GMV), with marketing at 8.2% of revenue, down 50bps YoY—key amid privacy headwinds.

By channel: paid search at 7.5x (Google Performance Max 40% of spend); social at 4.2x (TikTok/Instagram shoppable videos); RMNs at 6.8x (Amazon/Walmart sponsored). NA at 5.5x, Europe 4.9x, APAC 5.0x (India 8.1x).

Initiatives: ML bidding engine improved 22%; LiveRamp for first-party data; CTV testing at 3.8x. Q4 target: 5.5x.

On customer acquisition cost, our blended CAC was $28.50, down 12% YoY from $32.40, flat sequentially, with 1.2 million new customers (up 18% YoY). LTV at $185 yields 6.5x ratio, 4.8-month payback.

Channels: paid social $24 (42% mix), Google $32 (28%), SEO $12 (15%), affiliates $22. NA steady, Europe down 22% to €26, APAC $18. Pillars: ML models, incrementality tests, retention flywheel (42% repeat rate). Q4 CAC ~$30.

Finally, seller services and VAS revenue hit $1.82 billion, up 42% YoY, 28% of total revenue (gross margins 78%). Adoption at 68% (85% high-volume). Advertising $820M (62% adoption), fulfillment $550M (49%), payments $280M (58%), emerging $170M. NA 75%, APAC 61%, Europe 48%. Seller Central 2.0 lifts ARPU 15%. Q4: $2.1-2.3B.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on network throughput optimization and automation rollout, alongside last-mile partnerships. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs saw 15% unit efficiency gains. We are implementing AI sortation and AMR deployments across 12 FCs.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Performance Max campaigns and TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $28.50 with solid ROI. Our brand awareness increased by 15%. We are focusing on first-party data activation and incrementality testing.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, can you expand on the FCPO regional variances and how the Warsaw FC is impacting Europe?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. Jordan, want to take that?

Jordan Lee:
Absolutely, Alex. As I noted, Europe's FCPO at $8.76 reflects fragmentation and regs like France's anti-plastic mandates adding $0.30/unit, but the Warsaw FC and DHL partnership shaved 18 hours off cross-border times, saving 9% on express fees. We're targeting sub-$8 by year-end with MFCs in Manchester and Milan—early signs show 11% efficiency lift already.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong:
Great, thanks. Jordan, on take rate—how sustainable is the APAC expansion with promo normalization?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. APAC's 23.4% take rate, up 220bps, leverages Shopee-like dynamics where sellers pay for traffic; Indonesia/India GMV up 30% with minimal drag. Sustainability comes from ROP full rollout and stable promo at 13-15%—upside if cross-border premiums hold.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley.

David Ruiz:
Thanks. Taylor, with same-day penetration ramping to 35%, any supply chain risks tying back to fulfillment costs?

Taylor Kim:
Good question, David. Our MFCs enable 65% same-day/next-day, compressing last-mile to $2.10/order. Risks like parcel inflation are mitigated by VSIP contracts and dynamic routing—Q4 guidance holds firm at $7.05-7.15 FCPO.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Patel with Barclays.

Emma Patel:
Thanks, team. Riley, on ROAS—how are you navigating cookie deprecation in Europe?

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Emma. Europe's 4.9x ROAS uses server-side API tracking via Google Consent Mode v2, recovering 85% of signals. Clean rooms with Criteo/The Trade Desk bypass cookies entirely, and we're expanding RMNs there for resilience.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
